mzQuality features outlier detection, batch-correction using pooled study quality control samples (SQC), filters for removing unreliable compounds, various plots for inspecting, and generating reports
mzQuality is available as an interactive Shiny dashboard application called mzQualityDashboard.
Quality Control is an important step in the analysis of mass spectrometry data.
Existing tools phenomis and qmtools are designed with access to a phenotype in mind.
mzQuality was developed to perform outlier detection, batch correction and other quality control steps without the need for defined phenotypes.
mzQuality follows the recommendations of the mQACC for quality control by leveraging on proper batch design and the addition of various quality control samples.
mzQuality is capable of recommending different internal standards by exhaustively calculating the Relative Standard Deviation of QC samples (RSDQC) of batch-corrected ratios.
By supplying calibration line samples and known concentrations for spiked compounds, mzQuality is able to calculate absolute concentrations.
mzQuality features import of data from a variety of formats, including a generalized tab-delimited format and Sciex OS text exports.
phenomis provides tools for post-processing like quality control and normalization, as well as univariate statistics.
qmtools contains functions for processing quantitative metabolomics data, including imputation, normalization and filtering.
MatrixQCvis features interactive visualization of data quality metrics for various -omics datasets and uses the SummarizedExperiment object.
mQACC is the Metabolomics Quality Assurance and Control Consortium.
HUPO is the Human Proteome Organization.
HUPO has a Quality Control working group that focuses on quality control in proteomics.
mzQuality requires input data to be in a tab-delimited format.
The required columns for mzQuality input data include aliquot, compound, area, type, injection_time, and batch.
The readData function reads in data and checks for any missing or incorrect columns.
The buildExperiment function creates a SummarizedExperiment object from a data frame.
In the current version of mzQuality, only one sample type can be used for calculating concentrations.
mzQuality internally uses Bioconductor's SummarizedExperiment object to store data.
The buildExperiment function automatically calculates the compound / Internal Standard ratio for each sample and stores it in the ratio assay.
The convertExperiment function converts names in an already built SummarizedExperiment object to the ones mzQuality uses.

The doAnalysis function tests QC samples for outliers using their Compound / Internal Standard ratio. The doAnalysis function tests Study Samples for mis-injections using their Internal Standard areas
aliquotPlot shows the distribution of the selected assay per aliquot, colored per sample type.
The aliquotPlot can be used to inspect technical replicates for similar peak areas and peak ratios within a batch.
All plots in mzQuality can be faceted using the facetPlot function.
The facetPlot function allows faceting by any column present in colData.
compoundPlot is a scatter plot of a selected compound across samples.
PCA plot can be used to inspect variation within- and between batches.
In the PCA plot, Quality Control samples used for batch correction should ideally be centered and form a tight cluster.
The violin plot can be used to inspect the distribution of sample types.
The Concentration Plot shows a linear model based on calculated ratio and known concentration.
The createReports function creates a folder containing the results of analysis separated by Plots and Reports.
mzQuality is designed to be used by anyone with basic knowledge of R.
